newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX surges past 2,900 on surprise rally.
newsitem.headline: German DAX surges past 2,900 on surprise rally.

text.p: The German blue-chip DAX index opened floor dealings with an astounding 1.7 percent rally on Thursday to smash through the 2,900 mark for the first time in bourse trade.

The DAX surged 48.54 points to a bourse record of 2,914.61, stunning trade experts who had predicted profit-taking would hold off another run at the magical mark for at least another several trading sessions.
The DAX then paired gains slightly to stand up 46.87 points at 2,912.94 points by 1058 GMT.
The IBIS DAX hit an all-time high of 2,916.16 points.
The DAX rise was presaged on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones index recovered late on Wednesday to close down 19.75 at 6,422.94, well above the session's low of
Traders had been ready for a restrained bourse session in advance of a Bundesbank meeting later on Thursday. The central bank is not expected to lower rates and has scheduled no news conference.
"I am skeptical that we can hold at these levels. We need a consolidation. I must warm that it's not institutional investors who are leading this rally," said one Frankfurt trader.

But a report that Germany's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to post-unification high in November renewed hope that the Bundesbank could ease its stance against rate cuts in the coming months.

Unemployment totals added 50,000 to reach 4.1 million, on an adjusted basis, Germany's Federal Labour Office said. The adjusted rate rose to 10.7 percent, up from 10.1 percent in October, exceeding expectations.
German Bunds also rose on the unemployment data. March Bunds climbed 22 basis points to a high of 101.67 after the jobless figures arrived, havaing earlier touched a low of 101.32.
Meanwhile, the dollar held steady throughout the morning near 1.56 marks.
"The Bund future has been encouraged by job figures and the dollar has stablised at a high level," one trader said.

Car makers BMW AG and Volkswagen AG also surged, as both saw increases in November car sales in Japan. BMW, whose November sales in Japan climbed 41.5 percent, rallied 31 marks on the bourse to 1,079 by 1015 GMT.

Volkswagen climbed 6.50 marks on the bourse to 605, following a more than six mark jump in IBIS trading. VW's Japan sales rose 16.1 percent in November, although its Audi luxury unit saw a 5.5 percent drop.
